editorial_intent: Diagram how high-fat diet and aging cause the breakdown of Muribaculaceae microflora and short-chain fatty acids, leading to tight-junction protein disassembly, blood-brain barrier inflammation, and cognitive disruption.
subject: Colonic epithelial cell barrier composed of interlocking square tiles (ZO-1/occludin protein blocks) showing a left-to-right structural degradation, transitioning from tightly sealed blocks with dense carbohydrate-fermenting microbial lattices (Muribaculaceae) into broken, gapping gaps where jagged endotoxin forms pass through into a circulating stream of cytokine nodes.
setting: An ascending vagal nerve meridian line sweeping through the background as a geometric vector curve, intersecting an abstract botanical/microbial lattice motif rendered in muted mineral sage.
composition: Asymmetric Post-Constructivist lithograph on unbleached archival paper (#f8f4ec); left side displays an ordered, dense grid of mineral sage cellular blocks bounded by saffron ochre butyrate signals; right side displays fractured terracotta oxide gap-junctions releasing geometric endotoxin shapes toward an upper arc depicting hippocampal neural pathways.
